finding: Shared predicate producers reserved only mask byte backing, omitting the modeled typed-array view. Wider CASE choices and selectedRowIndexBuffer also omitted their view.
fix: Route 16 mask-allocation sites in batch.ts, batch-call.ts and dictionary-mask.ts through one allocator that validates extent and admits backing plus c.view before construction.
Charge the view for newly allocated wider CASE choice arrays; reused byte-mask choices keep the original view owner without double charging.
Charge the selected-index helper view and preserve temporary-index release after gather and physical output transfer.

contract.emptyMask: Still owns a typed-array view and therefore requires its view allowance.

validation.workerConcurrency: Only file startup is serialized; in-test concurrent queries remain concurrent.

evidence: Exact-cap/cap-minus-one tests cover empty and nonempty masks, independent retained owners, invalid extents and zero cleanup.
SQL logical/NOT/CASE/dictionary overlap tests retain only final output; 2/100-operand tests and 2/32/128-operand benchmarks preserve bounded mask count.
Numeric, bigint, timestamp, decimal, call and CASE paths include view charges while preserving scalar scratch limits, adaptive IN/decimal fallback and sibling isolation.
Physical selection/indices and gather tests cover overlap and temporary-index release.
Existing real HTTP and native R2 predicate/pressure fixtures exercise the updated allocation paths at 64/128 MiB caps.
boundaries: This changes modeled budget requirements by one existing c.view charge per allocated mask/index view; exact test capacities are derived from live overlap, not broadly relaxed.

Legacy gather output/vector conversion views, expression-plan metadata and other unadmitted vector helpers remain separate M1/F5 gaps. selectedRowIndexBuffer admission does not imply complete gather-output accounting.
Model charges are not exact VM/GC/native heap sizes. Whole-runtime headroom and final release acceptance remain open.
